description:
Dispatch reachability computes two things from one set of roots, and one of them wants a widening the other must not have.

`calculate_dispatch_reachability` seeds its roots with `Types::runtime_envelope`, which maps any var-carrying type to `any` at positive polarity. For the REACHABILITY DECISION that is correct and load-bearing: no runtime test can interrogate a type variable, so an unresolved variable must behave as "could be anything" or `intersect(var, target)` comes back empty and a reachable branch is wrongly pruned.

But the same roots are refined into `outcome_inputs`, and THOSE type each clause's parameters in `analyze_activation`. There a variable means NOT-YET-KNOWN, not "anything" -- graduating it to `any` discards a binding the fixpoint is still computing, and activation-input joins are cumulative so the `any` never retracts ([[unknown-is-not-none]]).

MEASURED on enum_take_drop_split (probe on the refinement, reverted):
  REFINE reduce_while_step/3 row=[[any], {:cont, {[any], :false}}, a2] outcome=OutcomeId(0) -> [..., any]
`a2` is the reducer slot -- an address var that NO test in reduce_while_step/3 looks at (it dispatches on slot 1's {:cont,_} vs {:halt,_}) -- and it comes back `any`. That row is then contributed to reduce_while_cont/3, whose reducer column becomes `any`, so `callable_value_clauses` returns None and value-typing EARNS `any` while the callsite summary resolved its targets precisely. The two disagree and materialization dies on the public_indirect_return_ty guard.

FIX (landed): envelope only the input ordinals some test in the plan actually reads. A slot that appears in no test cannot change any outcome, so it passes through unchanged and keeps its variable. Guards are conservative -- their inputs are not modelled, so a plan with guards envelopes everything.

Pinned by `a_slot_no_test_looks_at_keeps_its_type_variable`, and the pre-existing `bare_template_inputs_are_refined_as_runtime_values` still pins that a TESTED var slot does refine to runtime values.

HYPOTHESIS TESTED AND FALSIFIED, recorded so nobody repeats it: extending the same reasoning to vars NESTED beneath a tested subject (preserve the element of a tested list, the field of a tested tuple) causes 15 lib failures. Nested variables are load-bearing for the decision, not merely carried. So the untested-SLOT case is the safe boundary; anything deeper needs the type-model work in fz-f98.10, not a widening tweak.

SCOPE: this removes one class of var->any leak. It does NOT close enum_take_drop_split, which still fails on the same guard from a residual `[any]` arriving through a TESTED list slot (element widened by the envelope's recursion) -- that residual is fz-f98.10's variable-preservation core.
title: Dispatch reachability graduates untested input slots to any, poisoning the clause parameter types it also produces
